data_structures.text: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching a balanced binary search tree?
data_structures.explanation: A balanced BST has height ⌈log n⌉, so search touches at most O(log n) nodes.

data_structures.text: Which data structure operates on a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) basis?
data_structures.explanation: Queues process elements in FIFO order.

data_structures.text: What is the average time complexity for insertion in a hash table with good hashing?
data_structures.explanation: Hash tables offer average O(1) time complexity for insertion.

data_structures.text: Which traversal of a Binary Search Tree produces elements in sorted order?
data_structures.explanation: In-order traversal visits left subtree, root, then right subtree, yielding sorted keys.

data_structures.text: What is the worst-case space complexity of a Depth-First Search (DFS) on a graph with V vertices?
data_structures.explanation: The call stack in DFS can store up to V vertices in the worst case path.

data_structures.text: In a max-heap of size n, what is the time complexity of extracting the maximum element?
data_structures.explanation: Removing the root and heapifying down takes O(log n) time.

data_structures.text: Which memory allocation structure uses LIFO order for function call stack frames?
data_structures.explanation: Call stack frames are pushed and popped in Last-In First-Out order.

data_structures.text: What data structure is ideal for implementing prefix matching in autocomplete search?
data_structures.explanation: A Trie (prefix tree) stores string keys node by character, making prefix queries efficient.

data_structures.text: How many pointers does each node contain in a doubly linked list?
data_structures.explanation: Each node in a doubly linked list stores pointers to both next and previous nodes.

data_structures.text: What is the maximum balance factor allowed for any node in an AVL tree?
data_structures.explanation: AVL trees require height difference between subtrees to be at most -1, 0, or +1.

operating_systems.text: Which process scheduling algorithm can cause starvation for low-priority processes?
operating_systems.explanation: Priority scheduling can starve lower-priority processes indefinitely unless aging is used.

operating_systems.text: What state transition occurs when a process receives a hardware interrupt?
operating_systems.explanation: An interrupt preempts the running process, placing it back in the ready queue.

operating_systems.text: Which of the following is NOT a necessary condition for a deadlock?
operating_systems.explanation: No Preemption is a required Coffman condition; allowing preemption prevents deadlock.

operating_systems.text: What is thrashing in virtual memory management?
options: Excessive page faulting causing low CPU throughput
operating_systems.explanation: Thrashing occurs when the system spends more time swapping pages than executing instructions.

operating_systems.text: What synchronization primitive uses atomic wait() and signal() operations?
operating_systems.explanation: Semaphores use wait (P) and signal (V) integer operations for access control.

operating_systems.text: Which memory allocation algorithm suffers from external fragmentation?
operating_systems.explanation: Segmentation uses variable-sized segments leading to external fragmentation.

operating_systems.text: What is the purpose of the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)?
options: Fast hardware cache for page table translations
operating_systems.explanation: The TLB caches recent virtual-to-physical address translations for fast access.

operating_systems.text: In Unix system calls, what does fork() return in the parent process?
options: The PID of the newly created child process
operating_systems.explanation: fork() returns 0 to the child and the child's PID to the parent process.

operating_systems.text: Which page replacement algorithm suffers from Belady's Anomaly?
operating_systems.explanation: FIFO page replacement can exhibit more page faults when allocated more frame slots.

operating_systems.text: What is a Kernel thread compared to a User thread?
operating_systems.explanation: Kernel threads are directly scheduled and managed by the operating system kernel.

dbms_normalization.text: A relation is in First Normal Form (1NF) if:
options: Every determinant is a candidate key
dbms_normalization.explanation: 1NF requires scalar/atomic attributes without repeating groups.

dbms_normalization.text: What dependency does Second Normal Form (2NF) eliminate?
options: Partial functional dependencies on composite candidate keys
dbms_normalization.explanation: 2NF requires 1NF and no non-prime attribute depending on a proper subset of any candidate key.

dbms_normalization.text: To satisfy Third Normal Form (3NF), a relation must be in 2NF and have no:
options: Transitive dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys
dbms_normalization.explanation: 3NF removes transitive functional dependencies of non-prime attributes.

dbms_normalization.text: What condition distinguishes Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) from 3NF?
options: For X -> Y, X must be a superkey
dbms_normalization.explanation: BCNF requires that for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey.

dbms_normalization.text: Which normal form deals specifically with Multivalued Dependencies (MVDs)?
What anomaly occurs when removing a tuple unintentionally deletes other crucial data?
dbms_normalization.explanation: Deletion anomalies occur when deleting data causes loss of unrelated facts stored in the same row.

dbms_normalization.text: Which operation guarantees that a decomposed schema can reconstruct the original table exactly?
dbms_normalization.explanation: Lossless-join property ensures natural join of decomposed relations yields original relation.

dbms_normalization.text: What is a candidate key in relational databases?
options: A key that is chosen as primary key
A minimal superkey capable of uniquely identifying a tuple
dbms_normalization.explanation: A candidate key is a minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies tuples in a relation.

dbms_normalization.text: What is Fifth Normal Form (5NF) also known as?
dbms_normalization.explanation: 5NF is also known as Project-Join Normal Form (PJNF) and addresses join dependencies.

dbms_normalization.text: Why might a database designer intentionally denormalize a schema?
options: To improve read performance by avoiding expensive joins
dbms_normalization.explanation: Denormalization trades redundancy for faster query execution by reducing table joins.

ml_fundamentals.text: Which machine learning approach uses labeled training datasets?
ml_fundamentals.explanation: Supervised learning uses pairs of input features and ground-truth target labels.

ml_fundamentals.text: What phenomenon occurs when a model performs exceptionally well on training data but poorly on unseen test data?
ml_fundamentals.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise in training data instead of general patterns.

ml_fundamentals.text: Which metric measures the proportion of true positives among all predicted positive instances?
What is the primary purpose of K-Fold Cross Validation?
options: To obtain a robust estimate of model generalization performance
ml_fundamentals.explanation: K-Fold cross validation evaluates model stability across K distinct test splits.

ml_fundamentals.text: What does L1 Regularization (Lasso) encourage in model coefficients?
ml_fundamentals.explanation: L1 penalty adds sum of absolute weights, driving uninformative weights exactly to zero.

ml_fundamentals.text: Which algorithm is a non-parametric unsupervised clustering method?
ml_fundamentals.explanation: K-Means partitions dataset samples into K cluster centroids without labels.

ml_fundamentals.text: What tradeoff describes balancing model flexibility against sensitivity to small fluctuations in training data?
ml_fundamentals.explanation: High bias leads to underfitting; high variance leads to overfitting.

ml_fundamentals.text: What metric is computed as the harmonic mean of precision and recall?
What loss function is standard for binary classification models with probability output?
ml_fundamentals.explanation: Binary cross-entropy measures disagreement between predicted probability distribution and true binary target.

ml_fundamentals.text: In a Random Forest Regressor, how are individual decision tree predictions combined?
ml_fundamentals.explanation: Regression ensembles average output predictions of individual base estimators.

computer_networks.text: Which layer of the OSI model handles end-to-end communication reliability and flow control?
computer_networks.explanation: The Transport Layer (e.g. TCP) provides end-to-end reliability, sequence control, and flow management.

computer_networks.text: What protocol translates domain names like example.com into IP addresses?
computer_networks.explanation: Domain Name System (DNS) resolves human-readable names to IP addresses.

computer_networks.text: What mechanism does TCP use for flow control to prevent receiver buffer overflow?
computer_networks.explanation: TCP sliding window adjusts sender transmission rate based on advertised receiver window size.

computer_networks.text: Which protocol resolves IP addresses to physical MAC addresses on a local subnet?
computer_networks.explanation: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) maps IPv4 network addresses to Ethernet MAC addresses.

computer_networks.text: What is the subnet mask for a CIDR /24 network?
computer_networks.explanation: /24 CIDR prefix corresponds to 24 bits set: 255.255.255.0.

computer_networks.text: Which routing algorithm is based on Dijkstra's shortest path computation?
computer_networks.explanation: Link-state protocols like OSPF use Dijkstra's algorithm to compute shortest paths.

computer_networks.text: What is the standard port number for HTTPS traffic?
computer_networks.explanation: Port 443 is the well-known port reserved for HTTP over TLS/SSL (HTTPS).

computer_networks.text: What feature distinguishes UDP from TCP?
computer_networks.explanation: UDP is connectionless, offering low overhead without guarantee of delivery or ordering.

computer_networks.text: What technique allows multiple private IP addresses to share a single public IP address?
computer_networks.explanation: NAT rewrites source/destination IP/port headers to map private space to public IP.

computer_networks.text: What three-way handshake sequence establishes a TCP connection?
computer_networks.explanation: TCP establishment consists of client SYN, server SYN-ACK, and client ACK.

oop_concepts.text: Which OOP principle hides implementation details and exposes only an essential public interface?
oop_concepts.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data with methods and restricts direct internal access.

oop_concepts.text: What OOP feature allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method defined in its superclass?
oop_concepts.explanation: Method overriding allows a derived class to replace superclass behavior dynamically.

oop_concepts.text: What design guideline favors combining simpler objects over inheriting from a base class?
oop_concepts.explanation: Composition promotes flexibility and avoids tight coupling of deep class hierarchies.

options: A class that cannot be instantiated and may contain abstract methods
A class that implements all interfaces
oop_concepts.explanation: Abstract classes define common templates and signatures for subclasses without direct instantiation.

oop_concepts.text: What does the 'S' stand for in SOLID design principles?
oop_concepts.explanation: Single Responsibility Principle dictates a class should have one reason to change.

oop_concepts.text: What type of polymorphism occurs at compile time via method signature overloading?
oop_concepts.explanation: Compile-time (static) polymorphism resolves overloaded method calls based on argument signatures.

oop_concepts.text: Which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed in Java/C#?
oop_concepts.explanation: final (Java) or sealed (C#) prevents inheritance derived subclasses.

oop_concepts.text: What pattern decouples object construction from its representation?
oop_concepts.explanation: Builder pattern constructs complex objects step by step.

oop_concepts.text: What is the Diamond Problem in object-oriented programming?
options: Ambiguity in multiple inheritance when a class inherits from two classes with a common ancestor
oop_concepts.explanation: Diamond problem occurs under multiple inheritance when parent classes share a base class method.

oop_concepts.text: In OOP, what is a destructor or finalizer used for?
options: Releasing unmanaged resources when an object is destroyed
oop_concepts.explanation: Destructors clean up resources like file handles or sockets before object memory is reclaimed.

algorithm_design.text: What algorithmic strategy does Merge Sort utilize?
algorithm_design.explanation: Merge sort divides the array into sub-arrays, recursively sorts them, and merges results.

algorithm_design.text: What is the worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort with poor pivot selection?
algorithm_design.explanation: Quick sort degrades to O(n^2) when the pivot continuously selects minimum/maximum elements.

algorithm_design.text: Which algorithm computes single-source shortest paths in graphs with non-negative edge weights?
algorithm_design.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm efficiently solves single-source shortest path problems with non-negative weights.

algorithm_design.text: What strategy optimizes dynamic programming by storing results of subproblems?
algorithm_design.explanation: Dynamic programming stores subproblem solutions (memoization or bottom-up tabulation) to avoid recalculation.

algorithm_design.text: What problem asks for the minimum spanning tree of a weighted undirected graph?
algorithm_design.explanation: Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms find Minimum Spanning Trees (MST).

algorithm_design.text: What is the time complexity of searching an element using Binary Search on a sorted array of size n?
algorithm_design.explanation: Binary search halves the search space each step, achieving O(log n) time.

algorithm_design.text: Which graph algorithm can handle negative edge weights for single-source shortest path?
algorithm_design.explanation: Bellman-Ford algorithm handles negative weights and detects negative weight cycles.

algorithm_design.text: What algorithm design technique attempts locally optimal choices at each step?
algorithm_design.explanation: Greedy algorithms make top-down locally optimal decisions hoping to reach a global optimum.

algorithm_design.text: What complexity class contains decision problems verifiable in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine?
algorithm_design.explanation: NP (Nondeterministic Polynomial time) problems have solutions verifiable in polynomial time.

algorithm_design.text: What is the time complexity of Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path algorithm on V vertices?
algorithm_design.explanation: Floyd-Warshall uses three nested loops over V vertices, yielding O(V^3) complexity.

probability_stats.text: What is the probability of flipping two heads in a row with a fair coin?
What statistical measure describes the middle value of a sorted dataset?
probability_stats.explanation: The median divides ordered data into equal upper and lower halves.

probability_stats.text: According to the Central Limit Theorem, what distribution does the sample mean approach as sample size increases?
probability_stats.explanation: Central Limit Theorem states sample means converge to a normal distribution for sufficiently large n.

probability_stats.text: What formula calculates conditional probability P(A|B)?
probability_stats.explanation: Conditional probability P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B) for P(B) > 0.

probability_stats.text: What is the variance of a standard normal distribution?
probability_stats.explanation: A standard normal distribution ~ N(μ=0, σ^2=1) has mean 0 and variance 1.

probability_stats.text: In hypothesis testing, what is a Type I Error?
options: Rejecting a true null hypothesis (False Positive)
Failing to reject a false null hypothesis (False Negative)
probability_stats.explanation: Type I error occurs when the null hypothesis is true but falsely rejected.

probability_stats.text: What theorem relates P(A|B) to P(B|A), P(A), and P(B)?
probability_stats.explanation: Bayes' Theorem: P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B).

probability_stats.text: What discrete probability distribution models the number of events in a fixed time interval?
probability_stats.explanation: Poisson distribution models event arrival counts occurring at a constant average rate.

probability_stats.text: What is the relationship between Variance Var(X) and Standard Deviation σ(X)?
probability_stats.explanation: Variance is the square of standard deviation.

probability_stats.text: What does a correlation coefficient r = -0.95 indicate?
probability_stats.explanation: Pearson r close to -1 indicates a strong inverse linear relationship.

neural_networks.text: Which activation function outputs values constrained between 0 and 1?
neural_networks.explanation: Sigmoid σ(z) = 1 / (1 + e^-z) maps inputs into range (0, 1).

neural_networks.text: What algorithm computes gradients of loss with respect to neural network weights via the chain rule?
neural_networks.explanation: Backpropagation applies the chain rule backward from output to input to compute partial derivatives.

neural_networks.text: What problem plagues deep neural networks with Sigmoid activations during backpropagation?
neural_networks.explanation: Sigmoid derivatives (< 0.25) cause gradients to shrink exponentially in early layers.

neural_networks.text: What is the output formula for Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU)?
neural_networks.explanation: ReLU returns x if x > 0 else 0.

neural_networks.text: What regularization technique randomly deactivates neurons during training to prevent co-adaptation?
neural_networks.explanation: Dropout randomly sets a fraction p of node outputs to zero during training iterations.

neural_networks.text: Which neural network architecture is tailored for grid-like spatial data like images?
neural_networks.explanation: CNNs use convolutional kernels to extract local spatial features from images.

neural_networks.text: What layer normalizes intermediate activations across mini-batches to stabilize neural network training?
neural_networks.explanation: Batch Normalization standardizes mean and variance of layer inputs within each batch.

neural_networks.text: What optimizer combines adaptive learning rates for each parameter with momentum?
neural_networks.explanation: Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation) tracks exponentially decaying averages of past gradients and squared gradients.

neural_networks.text: What function converts raw logits into a multi-class probability distribution summing to 1?
neural_networks.explanation: Softmax exponentiates and normalizes logits across classes into valid probabilities.

neural_networks.text: Which mechanism allows Transformer architectures to weigh the importance of different sequence tokens dynamically?
neural_networks.explanation: Self-attention computes query-key similarity matrices to weight sequence token representations.

software_engineering.text: Which software development lifecycle model emphasizes iterative development in short sprints?
software_engineering.explanation: Agile/Scrum delivers functional increments in short 1-4 week iterations called sprints.

software_engineering.text: What type of testing verifies individual units or modules of code in isolation?
software_engineering.explanation: Unit testing checks individual functions/classes independently of external systems.

software_engineering.text: What does CI/CD stand for in DevOps practices?
software_engineering.explanation: CI/CD automates building, testing, and deploying software updates rapidly.

software_engineering.text: What design pattern defines a one-to-many dependency between objects so that when one changes state, all dependents are notified?
software_engineering.explanation: Observer pattern broadcasts state changes from a subject to registered observers.

software_engineering.text: In Git version control, what command creates a new local branch?
software_engineering.explanation: git checkout -b <branch> (or git switch -c <branch>) creates and switches to a new branch.

software_engineering.text: What architectural style structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services?
software_engineering.explanation: Microservices decompose systems into fine-grained, autonomous services over lightweight APIs.

software_engineering.text: What principle recommends writing tests before writing the corresponding production code?
software_engineering.explanation: TDD follows Red-Green-Refactor: write failing test, write minimal code to pass, refactor.

software_engineering.text: What term describes the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy solution now instead of a better approach?
software_engineering.explanation: Technical debt reflects future refactoring effort required to fix expedient code choices.

software_engineering.text: What type of testing evaluates system performance under extreme workload conditions beyond normal operational limits?
software_engineering.explanation: Stress testing pushes system bounds to determine stability and failure modes under heavy load.

software_engineering.text: What design pattern ensures a class has only one instance while providing a global point of access to it?
software_engineering.explanation: Singleton pattern restricts instantiation of a class to a single global instance.
